seoDescription: Learn how to add per-column search boxes to jQuery DataTables, including creating input placeholders from header text, wiring keyup/change handlers to column searches, handling differences between the legacy and new DataTables constructors (use API() with the old one), placing filters in header or footer, and preventing header input clicks from triggering column sorting—practical tips for building precise column-level filtering with DataTables and jQuery.

chapters.description: Show how to place inputs in the table header and prevent input clicks from triggering column sorting by stopping event propagation.

summary:
## Key Concepts

- **Per-column search inputs**: Create input elements inside table footer or header cells and use header text to build descriptive placeholders (e.g., "Search First Name").

- **DataTable instance reuse**: Store the DataTable reference in a variable (e.g., `dataTableInstance`) to reuse the API across loops and handlers.

- **Column mapping with index**: Loop through `tfoot th` elements and use the element's index to retrieve the corresponding `thead th` text via `.eq(index).text()` to ensure placeholders match columns.

- **Event handlers for filtering**: Attach `keyup` and `change` events to each input, then call `column(i).search( this.value ).draw()` to filter only that column.

- **Constructor compatibility**: There are two constructors — old (`dataTable`) and new (`DataTable`). The new constructor exposes the modern API directly. If using the old constructor, wrap the instance with `.api()` before calling newer methods (e.g., `.api().columns()`).

- **Header vs Footer placement**: Inputs can live in `thead` or `tfoot`; changing selectors moves the inputs. When placed in the header, clicking inputs can trigger column sort.

- **Preventing unintended sort**: When inputs are in the header, stop propagation on their `click` event (`e.stopPropagation()`) to prevent sorting when the input is focused.

> [!TIP] Use `.val()` inside the event handler to read the input value and `draw()` immediately after `.search()` to update visible rows.

> [!NOTE] Keep the input insertion and event wiring consistent with column order so indexes align between header and footer elements.

> [!IMPORTANT] If you see "columns is not a function" in console, check whether you're using the old constructor and, if so, call `.api()` before using the new column API.

## Takeaways

- Building per-column search requires creating inputs, mapping them to columns by index, wiring `keyup`/`change` to `column().search().draw()`, and handling constructor differences.
- For header inputs, prevent click propagation to avoid accidental sorting. These steps enable precise, column-scoped filtering with jQuery DataTables.
